quotes.text: If you build on a flawed starting point, even a high quality app becomes nothing more than structural compensation for a bad process.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that diagnosis must come before building.

quotes.text: Power Apps is the interface. Power Automate is the engine. Power BI is the eyes. Power Pages is the front door. Copilot Studio is the assistant.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable one-line mental model assigning each Power Platform tool its role.

quotes.text: This is why I always say that automation doesn't actually remove process problems, it just reveals them in an executable form.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes automation as a diagnostic that exposes ambiguous processes.

quotes.text: AI should sit on top of a stable process. It should never be asked to replace one.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear rule for placing AI assistants in the architecture.

quotes.text: Agents amplify clarity but they also amplify ambiguity, which is why I don't treat them as a separate strategy. I treat them as a multiplier applied to your existing design quality.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why agent value depends on the quality of the underlying design.

takeaways: Power Platform projects usually fail at the starting point, when a team picks a tool before naming the structural constraint in the process.
Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Power Pages and Copilot Studio each own a different layer, and data gravity, process criticality and identity and governance determine the right build order.
AI agents and Copilot Studio amplify whatever foundation exists, so stable data in Dataverse, executable processes and managed environments must come before the assistant layer.
hook: Most Power Platform solutions fail before anything is built, because teams name a tool before they name what is actually broken. This episode gives leaders, architects and makers a simple mental model for the five Power Platform tools and a repeatable sequence for choosing the right first move. Use it to stop building polished apps on top of broken processes.
